column3: The Hebrew has loves or caresses in the plural, rendered as singular “love.”
The name is poured-out perfume; “like” makes the metaphor a comparison.
The king has already brought her into his chambers, rather than the wish “May the king bring me.” The Hebrew speaks of remembering the caresses, rendered as “praise.”
The conjunction is and, rendered as “yet.”
The Hebrew says “my mare”; the BSB has no possessive.
The Hebrew says the eyes are doves; the BSB adds “like.”
The bed is green or luxuriant; “soft grass” is not explicitly named.
Houses is plural, rather than “house”; “fragrant” is not expressed.
